title: Mission: your own machine
drDigitalIntro:
Every computer you have used on this site was a drawing of one. This one is real — it is the machine you are sitting at.
• You will shrink this window and then make it fill the screen, and the page measures both as you do it.
• You will read your own battery level off your own screen and type it in. I check that against what your computer reports, so a guess will not pass.
• The rest is on your honor: opening an app, finding the clock, closing a window.
• Nothing here can go wrong. The worst outcome is a window left the wrong size, which you already know how to fix.

playgroundTask.goal: You ran the mission on your own computer

steps.say: Open any app on your own computer.
steps.detail: A notes app, a photo viewer, a second browser window — whatever sits on your dock or taskbar. Leave it open.

steps.say: Make this window small, then make it fill the screen.
steps.detail: Drag an edge or a corner to change the size. The numbers below come from the window itself, so they move as you drag.

steps.say: Find the battery on your own screen and type the percentage.
steps.detail: It sits along one edge of the screen, usually near the clock. Type just the number. If your computer has no battery — most desktop computers do not — type 100.

steps.say: Find the clock and the WiFi symbol on your own screen.
steps.detail: They live along the same edge as the battery. Knowing where that strip is means you can always tell the time, the connection and the charge at a glance.

steps.say: Close the app you opened, using its own close button.
steps.detail: The close button is on the window, not on the app's icon in the dock. Closing a window is not the same as quitting the program.

drDigitalSuccess: That was your machine, your window and your battery. No practice computer involved.
drDigitalHint: Take the window one at a time: shrink it clearly smaller than the screen first, then push it back out to the edges.
